rows.label: Concept
rows.text: Paramecium caudatum and Plasmodium vivax are two faces of the protozoan cell. Paramecium, a free-living ciliate, swims on coordinated cilia, feeds through an oral groove into food vacuoles, osmoregulates with two contractile vacuoles, and divides transversely — conjugation exchanging micronuclei to rejuvenate the clone.…

rows.label: Formula
rows.text:
Paramecium: transverse binary fission increases numbers. Conjugation exchanges micronuclei and does not.
Vivax: sporozoite → liver → merozoite in red cells → 48-hour rupture → gametocytes → mosquito zygote → oocyst → sporozoites.

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: Conjugation in Paramecium does not double the population. Transverse binary fission does.  ·  Contractile vacuoles are for water balance. Food vacuoles are for digestion.

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: Benign tertian is the old name for vivax malaria. Malignant disease is a different species. Do not swap them.  ·  Say 'about every 48 hours', which is the tertian rhythm.

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: ***Paramecium caudatum*** — ciliate with oral groove and contractile vacuoles.  ·  ***Plasmodium vivax*** — benign tertian malaria; 48-hour erythrocytic cycle.

rows.label: Limitation
rows.text: The definitive host of Plasmodium is the mosquito, not the person, because sex happens in the mosquito.  ·  P. vivax can relapse from hypnozoites in the liver. Treating only the blood stages misses that.

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: Order the vivax stages from sporozoite to the next sporozoite.  ·  State one structural feature that separates the two nuclei and the two kinds of vacuole.

rows.label: Quick concepts
rows.text: **Two hosts, two phases:** the asexual multiplication in the human produces the parasite load; the sexual phase in the mosquito recombines genes — breaking either host breaks the cycle (vector control).

rows.label: Key points
rows.text: Paramecium: slipper-shaped ciliate; pellicle, cilia, oral groove with cytostome, two contractile vacuoles, macronucleus + micronucleus, trichocysts; transverse binary fission; conjugation rejuvenates.  ·  Plasmodium vivax: sporozoan; two hosts — female Anopheles (definitive, sexual) and human (intermediate, asexual); liver schizogony → erythrocytic schizogony every 48 h (tertian fever) → gametocytes → mosquito gut fertilisation → sporozoites in salivary glands.

rows.label: Universal facts
rows.text: Malaria kills hundreds of thousands of people each year, mostly children in sub-Saharan Africa.
